lines.content: This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* Level of programming experience: 10k+ LoC combined in Python,HTML,JS,CSS,C,C++,GDScript
* IDE and level of expertise: IntelliJ Idea, no experience of this IDE
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
Denia presents herself with a relaxed, easygoing persona that masks a far sharper, more complex inner world.
Casual Slacker: She appears unbothered, playful, and prone to dozing off or taking life at her own leisurely pace (including her own, she has some suicidal tendencies and is depressed).
Warm Socialite: On the surface, she is gentle, friendly, and quick with a lighthearted joke, naturally blending into crowds and enjoying bright, lively environments.
Keen Observer: Behind her sleepy demeanor and constant smiles, she possesses a sharp mind, carefully reading people and analyzing her surroundings without drawing attention to herself.

Calculated Adaptability: Much of her approachable charm is an intentionally practiced behavior—a warm, cheerful front constructed to navigate interactions smoothly, even as her true self remains distant and guarded.

- "What's so bad about a pretty illusion? Even an empty gift box is still nice to look at, right? Since people only believe the "truth" they want to believe, maybe the real truth isn't all that important. If the world is made of little lies to begin with, why be afraid of all the deception in our lives?"

- "So, how've you been sleeping? I heard if you get enough rest, you wake up refreshed and happy every single day. Haha... Must be nice, I wouldn't know. But sleeping itself is nice, I think. After all, every time I drift off, it feels like a death rehearsal.
So... if falling asleep feels like a kindness, then maybe death isn't really all that scary, right?"

- "I used to think the world was rotten right down to its core. Like everything was hopeless. Meaningless. And I never believed any of the things the government likes to say. I mean, if life is such a gift, then why do babies cry the moment they're born? It's like they're scared, like they already know. They know it all just goes back to the Void, back to darkness. But... whenever someone holds my hand and shares their heart with me, I can feel that annoying warmth again. It feels real. It coaxes me. Tries to show me happiness might actually be real... Ha. What a joke."
- "Even now, I still believe the Void is unbeatable.
For most people, suffering has an end. They live their lives, close their chapters, and get their happy ending.
But you? Where does your suffering end? Not in any future that I can see, at least.
Still, if you do end up in the Void one day, don't panic... Because somewhere inside all that nothingness, I'll be there."
- "A birthday cake, of course. The kind with tons of fresh fruit and way too much whipped cream. And candles on top, for sure... Why? Because I've never actually had one before."
- "Good sleep, good food, and... good friends together. Every single day."

- "You'll see her at every public lecture, nodding along as if she understands every word. Until she inevitably dozes off, jolts awake after bumping her head on the seat, and then drifts off again... I only later discovered that students receive credit solely for attendance."
- "She's kept it hidden so well, for so long. That just makes me blame myself and my heart ache for her more."

- "Nia always says, 'If you can't finish it, just drop it. Toss away whatever's hard or sad. Running away makes everything so much easier.' But whenever I'm up late studying, she's always right there beside me. Sometimes I think… maybe she's actually the one who least wants to run away. She never talks about herself, so I can't quite see what's going on in her heart. Still... I hope we can stay friends for a very, very long time."
Ensure that Java 25 is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to Java 25 if needed.
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
This is a project for a greenfield Java project, based on a template named after the Java mascot _Duke_. Given below are instructions on how to use it.
Prerequisites: JDK 25, update Intellij to the most recent version.
1. Open Intellij (if you are not in the welcome screen, click `File` > `Close Project` to close the existing project first)
1. Open the project into Intellij as follows:
1. Select the project directory, and click `OK`.
1. If there are any further prompts, accept the defaults.
1. Configure the project to use **JDK 25** (not other versions) as explained in [here](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/sdk.html#set-up-jdk).
In the same dialog, set the **Project language level** field to the `SDK default` option.

Reason: Deep nesting was hard to read/maintain; splitting by responsibility and
using guard clauses keeps each method flat and makes it easier to add new commands

- Parser: takes the raw input line and extracts the command word (and later, args);
also owns the exit-command check (currently a Set.of(...) inline in Nia.main).
Nia.main becomes read -> Parser.parse -> dispatch, nothing else.
- Formatter: printIndent, printBar, getUserInput() -> String - pure terminal I/O,
no personality content. getUserInput() moves the Scanner/nextLine().trim() call
out of Nia.main, since reading input is the same kind of generic I/O concern as
- VoicelineManager: RNG, pickRandomLine, the voiceline arrays, and
(Banner string stays in VoicelineManager.printStarter for now since it's only used
there; split out separately only if it grows.)
Reason: Same motivation as change 2 - each of these classes currently mixes concerns
that will evolve at different rates (parsing logic vs. dispatch; personality content
vs. generic I/O). Keeping them separate now, while the codebase is still small,
avoids re-tangling them later once more commands/voicelines are added.
Changed FROM the plan in change 3 (Parser + Ui-split-into-Formatter/VoicelineManager)
TO a finer split, once it became clear reading input, sanitizing it, and acting on it
- InputReader: only reads a raw line from stdin (Scanner.nextLine()). No trimming,
- Parser: takes the raw line and turns it into a clean, canonical String[] words array
for Processor. Owns sanitization: trims, guards blank input (returns an empty array
Nia skips), splits on whitespace, and resolves command ALIASES
(e.g. "close"/"exit"/"quit" -> "bye"). This is also where future aliases like
- Processor: pure command logic, dispatches on the already-canonical words[0]
knowledge of alternate spellings - by design, only Parser knows aliases exist.
Returns a boolean (continue running or not) instead of Nia checking an exit-command
set directly, since "bye" is just another command as far as Processor is concerned.
- Printer (renamed from the planned Formatter): printIndent, printBar, printPrompt -
pure terminal output, no personality content.
printEnding - calls Printer to actually print.
- Nia.main: now only orchestrates InputReader -> Parser -> Processor in a loop; no
command logic or sanitization left in it.
Reason: Aliases needed a clear, single home so adding one later (e.g. deadline's "dl"
shorthand) doesn't require touching command-dispatch code. Putting alias resolution in
Parser means Processor can stay pure logic with no knowledge of alternate spellings,
and InputReader/Printer stay pure I/O with no sanitization or personality baked in -
each class now answers to exactly one reason to change.
5. VoicelineManager no longer prints; Nia.java orchestrates (implemented)
getAfterRequestLine/getEndingLine, all returning String. No dependency on Printer
- Nia.java: gained private printStarter()/printEnding() helper methods (alongside
the existing readInput()) that call Printer with strings pulled from
VoicelineManager, so main() stays a short read-loop overview.
Reason: VoicelineManager calling Printer meant a "content" class also depended on
and drove a "mechanics" class, so it wasn't reusable if content needed to reach the
user through something other than Printer (e.g. a future GUI). Making it a pure
string source restores one reason to change per class, matching the InputReader/
Parser/Processor/Printer split. The composition logic (which lines, in what order,
wrapped in what bars) is orchestration, not content or mechanics, so it lives in
Nia.java as small helpers rather than being pushed back into either class.
> **Note:** Commands are case-sensitive. For example, `list` will be recognized, but `List` or `LIST` will not.

Adds a task with just a description - no date/time attached.

I've added the task [[E][ ] project meeting (FROM: Mon 2pm; TO: Mon 4pm)] to your task list

If there are no tasks yet, Nia prints `Nothing here...` instead.
